Two people approached me - I knew one - and said they had this problem and whether I agreed that my name be put on the list of the party because there was the risk of the SDS being without a list on the upcoming elections. I agreed to be put on the list. And, at that moment, I didn't demand to be the first on the list nor was it offered to me. But these people who had come to make that request, at the last moment when they were supposed to submit the list, they simply put my name at the top. And I subsequently learned that I was the first on the list, but I didn't oppose that, although I -- it wasn't any condition of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks for that. Following the elections, were you appointed to any official position in the municipality of Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the elections, where the SDS fared second - the SDA was the strongest party - but the SDS was the second in the administrative structure the municipality of Ilidza, which meant that the president of the Executive Committee of the Ilidza municipality was a position that was given to the SDS. And the president of the municipality was a position that was filled by the SDA. They installed Mr. Mahmutovic. There was a formal contract between the administration and the Famos factory where I worked to the effect that I wouldn't attend my job at Famos during my term in office but when that expires I could return to my previous job at Famos.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks. I want to ask you about some of the persons or personalities who were involved -- elected to government in the municipality of Ilidza. Do you know a gentleman named Nedeljko Prstojevic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Nedeljko Prstojevic was a member of the Executive Committee -- or, rather, he was the secretary of the inspection inspectorate. It was a body of the Executive Committee, and I was president of that committee. I must add that I believe that, as soon as then, he was president of the municipal committee of the SDS for Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Maksim? Maksim Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know Mr. Maksim Stanisic very well. As a result of this same elections, he as representative of the SDS, became president of the Executive Committee at the level of the city of Sarajevo. The city of Sarajevo, you may know, is made up of ten municipalities. And at the level of all these ten, there's the administration that had an Executive Committee. The president was Mr. Stanisic, and one of these ten municipalities, Ilidza, I was president of the Executive Committee. And Ilidza was, as I said, one of the municipalities that made up Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in the period of time that you were working in the government of the municipality of Ilidza, did you ever attend any SDS party meetings in Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... okay --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: I went there as --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Following your election, how often would you go to -- to these meetings?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can say that I attended all meetings organised by the municipal committee of SDS of Ilidza because that was my obligation as president of the Executive Committee on behalf of the SDS and, in a way, the -- the one person in the municipality of Ilidza who -- who had the most prominent position for the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When you attended those meetings, did you ever become aware of instructions being issued to the SDS in Ilidza from higher organs or higher levels within the SDS?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: The SDS functioned the same way as all of the other political parties. It had its organisational structure at the top of which was the president and then there was the Main Board and there was the -- there were Municipal Boards. And as any organised party, it had precise instructions that were transferred to the level of Municipal Boards. And, of course, taking part in these meetings, I was acquainted with this basic organisational structure of the party and the way it functioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You speak there about precise instructions being received at the level of Municipal Boards. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what sort of precise instructions they were, whether they were documents or faxes, standing instructions, visits from members of the SDS from higher levels within the party?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's hard to speak at general level, but I can say that, with regard to the fact that it was a newly organised party, that it didn't have a structure that had already been stream-lined. Anyway, the instructions were mostly passed on orally from the members of the Main Board, that is, people who were members of the higher bodies of the party and who transferred that to the local levels to let them know what the expectations were of the party from the local level.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you ever addressed by a gentleman named Ostojic from the SDS Main Board?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic is a resident of Ilidza, that is, a citizen of the municipality in which I was president of the Executive Board. And there were frequent contacts between him and us at Ilidza. I don't remember any direct personal contact with him, but we did have some formal and informal contacts with him as a party cell, and we learned about the conclusions made at the higher party levels that we were supposed to implement. On the other hand, Mr. Ostojic was deputy prime minister, and the prime minister at the time was Jure Pelivan. Mr. Ostojic was his deputy and in charge of information, as far as I remember. So being a cabinet minister, he was in a position to act in the municipality of Ilidza and pass on conclusions from his purview because he was member of the cabinet of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And his first name?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Velibor. That was his first name. He is dead now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: This would be an appropriate time, if Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. So we take the break now and return in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Kezunovic, you mentioned that this gentleman Mr. Ostojic would occasionally address you or communicate with you at the Ilidza municipal level; he, being on the SDS Main Board. Did Mr. Jovo Jovanovic ever do the same?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovo Jovanovic, at the time, was president of the town board of the SDS as far as I remember, and in accordance with the logic of things he occasionally came to Ilidza to take part in the activities of the party and attend some meetings to learn about the activities. And that's why he occasionally came to Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And that communication and transfer of information, was it just one way, from the top down; or did your municipal Ilidza board also brief him and such personality -- other personalities in the SDS hierarchy on events on the ground? What was happening in Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. It is logical for that communication to go two ways, and we did information about the decisions of the higher bodies of the party, and there was opportunities for the members of these higher bodies to become acquainted with the events at the local level - in this case, Ilidza - and which may necessitate the taking of political decisions that would be applied more generally and not only to Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown 65 ter 1972, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. This document, it's clear what it is. It purports to come from the Main Board of the SDS, and it's addressed to Municipal Boards of the SDS in Bosnia. And it sets out operational guide-lines concerning the holding of meetings of the local boards and the necessity for local boards to remain in contact with the people, with households. And it purported to also attach a questionnaire which is not on the document. My question is this: Were you aware of any such instructions concerning the holding of meetings, the weekly review of the situation, the need for local boards to keep in touch with the people in specified numbers of households?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: I haven't had the opportunity to see this document. I cannot speak specifically about it. But, generally speaking, yes, there have been activities of the party as outlined here. I cannot say anything about any particular outcomes of this document that we see on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say you haven't seen this document, you mean that you didn't see it back in the early 1990s but you've seen it since coming to testify?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, if Your Honours please, I would seek to either tender that document; if you're not with me on that, then I would ask that it be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that there are no grounds for tendering this document through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, apart from the lack of nexus, I'm not sure I appreciate what is being -- for what purpose it's being tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: To establish the connection between local boards of the SDS and the Main Board of the SDS and the communications and the gathering of information and the passage of information up to the SDS Main Board. That's the -- that's the main purpose of -- of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Save for the architecture of the -- perhaps architecture is the wrong analogy, but the mechanics of how these levels operated is -- doesn't it go without saying? I mean, do we need a piece of paper to lay that down?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, it does bolster that. And it is evidence of that, And that's the point I'm trying to nail. But if Your Honours feel that it's superfluous, I would ask that it simply be marked for identification at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... pending what? We don't appreciate the relevance or indeed for this document, Mr. Di Fazio. And we decline to admit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You mentioned that --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, just bear with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You mentioned that there had been activities of the party as outlined here in the document. Did your board actually -- actively seek out information about what was happening in Ilidza and specifically transfer that to other levels of the SDS further up the hierarchy?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot speak about any particular activities that were the outcome of this document that we've seen. But the party did have activities that relied on communication between the various levels of the party. And, of course, these were of interest to the local community of Ilidza. I cannot single out any particular event of this type. That would have flown out of this document that we've just seen, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown 65 ter 20, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: This document is a decision on appointing a regionalisation staff, and it refers to various members of that staff. And you head it as president. And can you see that on the second page of the document of the English, at least. And you can see it on the first page of the B/C/S. The purpose of the document -- or, rather, of the -- of the staff is to monitor the implementation of a decision which relates to - and I quote: "The disassociation of populated areas from one municipality and their incorporation into another municipality." Firstly, were you a member of any such regionalisation staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How did that come about?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: To explain the genesis of the regionalisation staff, we would have to go back to that time. I believe it was 1991. Yes, September 1991. After the population census which was conducted in April 1991, and once events in Bosnia-Herzegovina started going their way, namely, foreboding future misunderstandings, the parties, including the SDS, started considering political moves, concrete moves, to be taken to ease the situation, to reduce tensions. And the ethnic structure of Bosnia-Herzegovina was one of the crucial problems in this respect. The population census being completed, we used the information contained therein to come up with an ethnic image of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I tried to restructure the then-Bosnia-Herzegovina from the top to the bottom - and Bosnia-Herzegovina was still part of Yugoslavia then - in order to prevent future problems. The purpose of this regionalisation committee, or commission, was to come by data that should be used as the foundation for a proposal toward preventing potential problems in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. The document says that one of the members of the staff was Mico Stanisic from Pale. Is that the Mico Stanisic who later became minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever work with him on this particular staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can say that the staff -- or, rather, I don't remember its being constituted. I don't remember being certified as a member of that staff. Only the initial steps were taken, but it wasn't formally constituted. And I don't remember a meeting attended by Mr. Stanisic. Actually, I barely know Mr. Mico Stanisic. And we met not in the framework of this regionalisation staff, which never really met to constitute it, but I met him informally on other occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you remember when in relation to September 1991 you met him?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've been thinking since yesterday. I remember a meeting which was accidental in the -- in the office of the then-Speaker of the Assembly Momcilo Krajisnik. I can't remember how this accidental meeting occurred, but I remember we met in that office with several people, and, among other people, there was Mr. Stanisic. I believe that was the first time we met. And he will probably remember that he and I and all the others were listening to a presentation by a professor at the faculty of economics, Aleksa Milojevic [phoen], about the structure of the city of Sarajevo; as such, its urban and rural position, the structure of the population in both the urban and the rural parts of Sarajevo. And he said that in the urban area the Muslim population was in the majority; whereas, in the rural parts, the Serbs and the Croats were in the majority, and what the implications of that were. So we were listening to that presentation, and it was in the context of what we discussed before. It was a meeting where Mico Stanisic and I were practically just attendees.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm sorry. 54, 20, I believe the witness specifically explained which kind of implications. Naming where the professor came from, which faculty. Maybe this can be explored.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You heard what Defence counsel said. Did you mention anything in relation to where the -- which faculty the professor came from?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: You're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, it was missed in translation.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: I said that I practically remembered the occasion when Mr. Mico Stanisic and I met. It was an informal meeting in the offices of the then-speaker of the Assembly, and the professor was -- yes. The faculty of economics in Sarajevo. Aleksa Milojevic is still a full-time professor of economics there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe the witness said economic implications of that situation. That is what I was referring to. "Economic implications." If he can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, did you mention anything about economic implications in your previous answer?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What did you say? Because we missed it.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: I tried to remember that meeting. In that context during that informal meeting, we were listening to the thoughts of Professor Aleksa Milojevic on the topic of what the then-structure of Sarajevo, its rural an urban parts, was and what are the implications for the economic life of the town of Sarajevo and what the city of Sarajevo should do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please instruct the witness to talk slower because this is really creating a problem, I assume, for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of any problem, but if that is a problem, then, witness, please just go a little slower so that the interpreters have time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, earlier you mentioned that you were going to use the census, the results of the 1991 census, to do some work in relation to the duties of this regionalisation staff. How were you going to -- how -- what precisely were you going to do?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I call the census -- is that census in 1991. Regrettably, we didn't have any other in Bosnia-Herzegovina, but that census was an opportunity to gain an insight into the overall situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, including the ethnic aspect and the entire structure of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And, using this data, we tried to analyse it for the purpose of formulating proposals that would be useful, for eventually overcoming the situation that prevailed in Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You say "we." "We tried to analyse it," the census data, "for ... formulating proposals." Are you referring to the work of the regionalisation staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: No. I meant primarily, first of all, the municipality of Ilidza, since I, as the president of the Executive Board, was at the same time president of the commission for the census. And I engaged a whole team in my Executive Board. And the job of these people was to analyse the data derived from the census and, on that basis, try to formulate specific proposals that would be geared at changes in the administrative structure of the town of Sarajevo. And that was a proposal that was to be adopted at the level of the city of Sarajevo and then, later, perhaps, after further analysis, be raised to the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was Predrag Bejatovic from Vogosca a member of the regionalisation staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the man, but I don't remember that he was a member. Because that founding session of the board never took place, so I don't remember the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you know any of these other gentlemen, apart from Mico Stanisic who you've told us about, as being members of any regionalisation staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Tell us about them, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: I know Mr. Prstojevic; I remember him. Radislav Unkovic from Novi Grad municipality. Mico Stanisic I've already mentioned. Mr. Slobodan Jovandic. Jovandic, that's an architect in the institute for urbanisation; I know him and no one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did any of them do any work that you're aware of on a regionalisation staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Preparations were done as a result of the census in a way that was agreed at the time: Namely, that within the framework of the institute for city development, all this data should be agglomerated at the level of the city of Sarajevo; that it should be analysed in the institute, including one detail from that paper, ethnic maps of the city. And the man who was in charge, then, of this job in the institute was Mr. Jovandic, an architect, and he was supposed to transpose that onto visible maps. And that was done, also at the level of the board, as preparation for the work of this committee for regionalisation. But that was also the end of the activities because no further work was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I seek to tender the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1467, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And you mentioned earlier a meeting that you had with Mr. Mico Stanisic in Mr. Krajisnik's office, and you also said you didn't know him very well. Apart from that meeting that you've mentioned in Mr. Krajisnik's office, did you ever meet with Mr. Mico Stanisic on any other occasions that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Not that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Eventually, in 1992, did a Serb municipality of Ilidza come into being?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The establishment of the Serbian municipality of Ilidza followed the establishment of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in early January 1992, speaking of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And soon after that, the Serbian municipality of Ilidza was also established, meaning that a meeting was held where this was decided and verified that the Serbian municipality of Ilidza should be established as a result of a decision that had already been made at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just yes or no: Did you attend that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you hold any position in the Serbian municipality of Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In that Serbian municipality of Ilidza, I was elected president.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did it actually sit and conduct sessions in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot talk about April. I cannot remember clearly what happened in April, but I think that after that first session, where people were elected to the main posts, I don't remember calling another session as president of the Serbian municipality of Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. Can you quickly --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can we quickly have a look at 65 ter 3087, please. Thanks. And if we could just please go to the B/C/S version, perhaps to the last page -- second page, rather -- or the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is that your signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. This is dated 3 January of 1992, and it's the decision to proclaim the municipality that you've -- Serbian municipality of Ilidza that you've just been talking about. And it says that this happens partly as a result of the constitution, and partly as a result of the will of the Serbian People, and partly as a result of an instruction from the Main Board of the SDS dated 19 December 1991. Do you have any knowledge or memory of that particular instruction, number 079, of 19 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think that instruction was mentioned when we were making this decision. But I don't think I held that decision on -- sorry, instruction on paper. I didn't need it at the time either because all the key protagonists in the establishment of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina attended this meeting as well, and that decision by the supreme organs of the party and the then-Serbian authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina was conveyed to us, namely, that municipalities were to be formed, in municipalities where the right conditions have already been met.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So even though you may not have had the actual document, instructions number 79 of 19 December 1991, the import, the meaning of the decision, was conveyed to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. The document says that the Assembly has got to consist of Assemblymen from the SDS, presidents of local boards, or Assemblymen of Serbian ethnicity who signed a statement. You've told us you weren't in the SDS. Did you sign a statement in order to become a member of the Assembly, or you can't recall? I'm referring there to -- to Roman numeral III, paragraph 3; can you see it there.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: You see, as president of the Executive Board, I couldn't be an Assemblyman. These two are not compatible. There is a separation between the executive authorities and the parliament, and I was the local prime minister practically, so I couldn't sign a statement, nor could I become a member of that parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: At the meeting where the Serb municipality of Ilidza was created, did Mr. Jovanovic, the Mr. Jovanovic -- Jovo Jovanovic that you spoken of earlier, did he attend?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: I really cannot be sure now. I think he was there, but I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I tender the document, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1468, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown 65 ter 3088, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The document refers to Serbian volunteers under heading - paragraph 1, number 1 - heading 1. Who are these Serbian volunteers being referred to there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: This is January 1992. These are Serbian volunteers who were, by that time, already engaged and participated in the combat that was drawing to an end in Croatia. And they were people from the Ilidza municipality; some of them I knew got killed, leaving families behind. And, of course, their families approached us for resolution of their status and various benefits. And in my role as president of the Executive Board of the Serbian municipality of Ilidza, I had to try to find solutions or make proposals how to help out these families.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. It also says under number 3 that steps were to be taken to protect the interests of the Serbian People in Ilidza, which included the protection of workplaces and other spiritual and material assets in the Ilidza municipality. Do you know what the appropriate steps were to be, what was envisaged?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: As you can see, it was a draft decision. We made an initiative to have some measures adopted at a higher level. And in January 1992, it was a time on the eve of a very tumultuous event in Ilidza and in the whole of the country; we were feeling the consequences of the war in Croatia; and, of course, there was prevailing fear of the war spreading to us. And we were trying to draft proposals and take preventive measures to stop the war from spreading to Bosnia-Herzegovina in the same form.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I seek to tender that document into evidence if Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If it was only a draft which was never implemented, the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... are we missing something? Am I missing something, Mr. Di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It is evidence of the commencement of functioning. It might have been a draft, but it was up for consideration. Obviously they took time to create the document. And it is evidence of this particular Ilidza municipality functioning to a -- at least to -- to that extent where they are considering draft decisions. If you don't think that you would served by it, then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Was it ever passed and adopted?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I can ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was it ever passed and adopted?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: You're asking if the proposal was approved; it was. But I don't know of any consequences that this proposal may have had. I don't know that as a result of this proposal any decision was made at higher levels of the party or Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So the document remains an example of the functioning and work of this particular municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Except that the witness's answer, what he just volunteered, answers the reservations that I have about accepting this document in evidence. Because -- it was -- it was the -- an example of the -- of the formulation of an intention, but it didn't go any farther than that. Nothing happened as a result of it. So therefore I don't see how, down the road, there is anything that you can invite the Chamber to deduce from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Other than the fact of the functioning of the -- of the -- of the Ilidza municipality, Serbian municipality of Ilidza. Other than that. I agree that the witness has already testified about the functioning and its setup and how it started to work. This merely bolsters that. It's that -- to that extent, it's not a ground-breaking document; but, to that extent, it corroborates his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We're not persuaded, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I asked you about the -- the Serbian municipality of Ilidza. Did there come a time when a Crisis Staff was created in Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff was established in Ilidza but not as a result of a decision by the Serbian Assembly or anything. It happened as a result of the events that started after the month of April. The Crisis Staff was set up, indeed, but it had nothing do with the activities of the Serbian municipality of Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How was it set up? As a result of what, I should say, was it set up?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: As a result of the new circumstances. In May, as you know, there was an escalation of the conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the party then instructed all Municipal Boards to go forward with organising defences. And Crisis Staffs were established as a part of that activity throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina, both in areas where Serbian municipalities were organised and in other municipalities; in which case, the -- the party apparatus took care of that, rather than the municipal authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You say the party issued the instructions for Municipal Boards to go ahead and create Crisis Staffs. When you say "the party," I know you're talking about the SDS, but do you know what part of the party? Is it the Main Board or some other organ within the party?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot speak of specific decisions. In any case, instructions came that in every municipality Crisis Staffs should be set up. And every Municipal Board took steps to do that. And in such a way, through the party the, the Crisis Staff of Ilidza was also set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you a member of the Crisis Staff in Ilidza; and, if so, what was your position?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Ex officio I was a member of that Crisis Staff. It operated -- started from April, I think; and I was member of the Crisis Staff until the movement when I resigned from all my posts in the party and in the municipality which was in early May. So I was a member of the star for about a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And can you just be a little more specific about when the Crisis Staff started to function. You told us April, but do you know when in April? If you don't, that's fine. But if you can give us a more accurate idea ...

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: I really cannot remember the exact date, but I think it was in the beginning of April. I don't know when.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Tomo Kovac?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tomo Kovac was commander of the uniformed police in Ilidza municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was he a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Tomo Kovac was a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: By virtue of what? What reason was he a member of the Crisis Staff in Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, ex officio, he was a policeman. It was traditional law enforcement activity. And the Crisis Staff was supposed to take care of the security and safety in the municipality of Ilidza. And that, by definition, was the job of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So because he was a police officer -- because he was the -- in the police, that was the reason why he was in the Crisis Staff; do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. As police commander, he was member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you about every member of the Crisis Staff in Ilidza but just one in particular. Was a gentleman named Ljubo Bosiljcic a member of the Crisis Staff in Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Ljubo Bosiljcic was a member of the Crisis Staff, if I remember well; also ex officio because at the time he was deputy to the National Assembly, actually the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina. He died just ten or 15 days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Still talking about this period of time in February and March - and I'd like to get through this quickly - you -- I'll lead you to this extent: You've mentioned in your statement that there was an episode involving a flag in the municipality, erected above the municipality building. Can you tell the Trial Chamber about that particular episode?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: It's a Serbian flag that was hoisted on the building of the Assembly, and I want to say that this episode practically marks and colours the atmosphere that prevailed in Ilidza and in the city of Sarajevo and further afield. To explain this problem, I have to say that Tomo Kovac in the police, on the one hand, and people who represented the -- who represented the municipal authorities, the president of the municipality, Mr. Mahmutovic and I, we were trying at that time to return, to recover that atmosphere; and we expected and we were convinced, me most of all, that excalation of the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina is completely impossible and should not happen. And the four of us tried to make an agreement to have that municipality, for which we were responsible, protected by our own activities, by our own actions, from adverse events. And we often found ourselves in situations where we had to diffuse tensions in the municipality. And in most cases, we were successful. And that's how it happened that adverse consequences started in Ilidza later than in the rest of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... okay --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: And that's how the Serbian flag, one day, alit upon the building of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The Serbian flag was erected on -- above the municipal building in Ilidza. Can you tell the Trial Chamber approximately when that event took place?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: It will be difficult for me to mention a date. I believe that it was in mid-March or toward the end of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And this was a building that --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: It's the municipal -- municipality building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And at the time, the police in Ilidza, had they split and divided with Serbian police officers operating independently from their Muslim and Croatian counterparts?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot assert that explicitly, whether there had been a formal division. But there was some policemen, Mr. Mljivic [phoen] and Mr. Kovac, they worked in the same building as I. And we could all feel the adverse events in Ilidza. I really cannot say whether there was an official division or split in the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina because I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks. Did you approach Mr. Kovac about the presence of this flag; and, if so, briefly tell us what his response was.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. I went to work and immediately noticed. And I reacted because it was not in keeping with the spirit of our agreement to keep the municipality of Ilidza outside the scope of possible conflicts. And I spoke to the commander of the station, Mr. Kovac, to have the flag removed from the municipality building. He explained to me it wasn't possible because the police hadn't put the flag there and that the police basically couldn't remove it. I insisted that this be done and asked one policeman to be given to me, and he did. So, assisted by that policeman, I removed the flag. And that was the end of that episode with flying the Serbian flag from the building of municipality which was, at the time, the municipality of both -- over both Serbs and Bosniaks -- or rather, Serbs, Bosniaks, and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'll ask you now to look at another document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: 65 ter 2350. Perhaps the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, I'll -- you can see what this document says it is. It's not -- purports to be. It's a list of members of the Main Board of the SDS. And I want to take you through some of the names. Tell us if you know them. Number one you obviously would know: Dr. Karadzic; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And number 5 is a gentleman I think you've spoken about earlier --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the late Mr. Ljubo Bosiljcic, deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And number 11, you do know him: Bozidar Vucurevic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, 11. Bozidar Vucurevic. He was -- at the time, he was the president of the Municipal Assembly of Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Velibor Ostojic; you've spoken about him this morning. You obviously know him. And --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- number 31: Mico Stanisic; you obviously know him. Some other names, if -- on the next page of the English. And I'm looking at number 34: Jovan Tintor; do you know him?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Jovan Tintor is a well-known name. He is from Vogosca, near Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: 35, Savo Ceklic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him -- I didn't know him well, Dr. Savo Ceklic, but it was a well-known name to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Then the last three names, for the same of getting through this quickly: Tomislav Sipovac, number 37; 39, Jovo Jovanovic; and 40, Petko Cancar. Did you know them?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were they all members of the Main Board of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: I really cannot say. But as far as I remember, they should have been members of the Main Board because they were active and well-known people. Most probably they were members of the Main Board. At that time, certainly. I can't see a date here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours, please, I would ask that this document be marked for identification at least at this stage. It may be that -- possible to acquire further evidence about membership of the Main Board of the SDS, and it would be a useful document from that point of view. And, of course, the witness has already spoken about it and mentioned some of the people on it who he believes were members of the Main Board of the SDS by virtue of their position. So that, at least, would warrant, I suggest, marking it for identification at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1469, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can we now look at 65 ter 2351.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And, Mr. Kezunovic, I want to go through essentially the same exercise again once that's up on the screen. And in Cyrillic the numbers are: Number 1, Radovan Karadzic, you've mentioned; and number 4, Ljubo Boskjcic, you've mentioned. Number 14, Sveto Lucic; did you know that person?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sveto Lucic is a man from Pale whom I know, and I knew him then too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And continuing, you've mentioned number 17, Velibor Ostojic. What about number 18, Boro Sentic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Number 19 --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Boro "Sentic;" this is a typographical error. It's "Sendic" with a D. He's a well-known member of the SDS and a member of the Main Board, and I was -- believe he was one of the very prominent members of the party from Banja Luka, and he was very active for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sendic.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sorry -- Sendic --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- number 18; you know for sure that he was a member of the -- of the Main Board. It's not that you were -- [Overlapping speakers] ... or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Oh that. No, I didn't say that. I knew for sure that he was member of the Main Board. I just know Mr. Sendic, and I know his activities. But whether he was an official member of the Main Board, I don't know because I have no grounds for claiming that. I had no chance to see these documents. But I suppose that was -- probably he was a member of the Main Board because he was a very prominent member of the party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you speak very fast, and I can hear from the interpreters that they have a hard time following you. So please speak a little more slowly. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And if the list continues with what is, on the face of it, supposed to be membership from 1991 -- and names that I want to run past you there are Bozidar Vucurevic; you know that person? Number 5?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I can't see what you're referring to. Number 5 ... you mean the previous list?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No. The list continues with a list of --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- for 1991, and it starts -- it's the same document, but it continues from 1991. And the one -- the names I'm going to run past you are from that second part of the document. Starting with number 5: Bozidar Vucurevic; do you know him?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I've already said who Mr. Vucurevic is --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you may have, and I --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: -- and I said that most probably he was a member of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm sorry, if I -- can you repeat them? I can't remember all of them, so it will be more efficient to get through them quickly. Number 7, Rajko Dukic; do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I think the shorter way of getting this information into evidence is probably to ask the Defence if any of this is contested. Because if it's not, then let's just admit the lists and move on. Can the Defence identify whether they contest the information in these lists?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we are opposed to introducing this document through this witness because this witness is not a member of the SDS, nor is he a member of the Main Board of the SDS. And he has explicitly said that he cannot state with certainty whether or not the persons on the list are members of the Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party. He supposes things, but he doesn't know. The only thing he said is that he knew some of these persons in person. He doesn't know them in the capacity of members of the Main Board, but he knows them personally. This is our basic objection, the basic objection of the Defence. So we believe that, at this moment, this document cannot be introduced through this witness, nor can we try to elicit details of -- about this document from this witness, except for what he said, that he personally knows Bozidar Vucurevic. But that isn't of much use to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cvijetic. I suppose we could MFI the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's as far as I want to go, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So let's do that and move on because this is a waste of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So it's marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1470, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kezunovic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm Slobodan Cvijetic, and I'm Defence counsel of Mico Stanisic. I'm going to ask you some questions. Although you were not a member of the Serbian Democratic Party, you could and should know that the SDS, at the beginning, during the preparations for multi-party elections, in fact, was a movement of the Serbian People, which, as it was claimed at the time, had assembled all patriots and also people who were anti-Communists which was also said at the time. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't totally agree with the way you put this. I didn't really observe anti-Communism, at least not that it wasn't that pronounced. But certainly the SDS was the largest political organisation of the Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina which was established last, after the SDA and the HDZ. So, before the elections, they didn't have enough time. So they had a hard time organising themselves to run at all. So, in that respect, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You will agree with me, won't you, that such a party, in that initial appearance, one -- and later, when it entered government, basically cleansed its membership, introduced membership cards, and set up a genuine organisational structure once it became a relevant political factor in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I've already mentioned that the Serbian Democratic Party was under time pressure to meet the deadlines to run in the elections, and that was the 24th of November, 1991. There were shortcomings in the organisation of the party, but these shortcomings were -- could be overcome later. They had to organise and structure their membership.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let me take you back to the documents showed to you by Mr. Di Fazio toward the end so we can confirm what we are a speaking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us see 65 ter 2351 again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It's a list, at least that's what it's called, of the Main Board of the SDS for 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And let us turn to page 2. Yes. And let's start with 1991. Let's go to the lower half of the page. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We reviewed this document together. That's why I can ask this question directly to you. Did you observe that the members who were -- who were mentioned under the heading for 1990 can no longer be found under the heading for 1991? Did you observe that when we looked at the document together? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it can be seen from the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did you observe the same thing I did, namely, that Mr. Stanisic cannot be found under the heading for 1991. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we established that together.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Let me take you back to the previous document used by the Prosecutor, namely, 65 ter 2350.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are on channel 6, but had English in our heads.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: That's interpreter's apology. I advertently pressed the wrong button.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must say something whether to -- to check whether we are getting Serbian now. Now we're not getting anything. Now we can hear. It's okay now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kezunovic, look at the remarks on the list of the members of the Main Board from 1990. You can see it in the lower part of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll down so we can read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do read these remarks.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: It should be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the witness would like it to be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We looked at them yesterday.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Remark: Members of the Main Board --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You don't have to read it out aloud. Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can you see the reason why Mr. Stanisic cannot be found under the heading for 1991? Because according to this remark his name hasn't been circled and his term in office has not been extended. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC
utterances.text: By what I see written here, what you say is very probable.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just commented on two documents used by the Prosecution, and I believe -- I think that this would be a convenient moment because our time is running out, and I am now planning to deal with a different topic and show the Defence exhibits to the witness. So I'll hardly be able to start. With your leave, I would then stop off today and continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Kezunovic, we're about to take the adjournment for today. Having been sworn as a witness, you cannot have any communication with the lawyers from either side; and should you -- in any conversations you have with anybody outside of the courtroom, you cannot discuss your testimony. So we will resume in this courtroom tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 23rd day of June, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.41 p.m.,
